reviewed_by: Governance v3 multi-provider skill audit (task audited-skills-stack-v3). All 33 upstream skills under skills/ plus the repo-local .agents/skills/ce-skill-work were read with their complete dependency closures; every bundled script was read end to end.

license.notes: MIT requires the copyright and permission notice to accompany all copies, so the upstream root LICENSE is copied verbatim into every vendored skill directory (origin=local, with a reason) rather than relying on a single shared notice.

notes: 22 of upstream's 33 skills are vendored; 10 are excluded and 2 are held (see excluded_skills[]). Upstream deliberately DUPLICATES shared components into each owning skill rather than factoring them out, and pins the duplicates with byte-parity tests, so each vendored skill directory is self-contained: there is no shared runtime tree to install alongside it. Verified at this pin: no skill references a sibling skill's files and no skill uses ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}. Every bundled script is located via an inline SKILL_DIR anchor and invoked through an explicit interpreter, so normalizing file modes to 100644 breaks no invocation.

excluded_skills.name: ce-product-pulse
excluded_skills.reason: Generates time-windowed product-usage reports from configured product-analytics, tracing, and payments providers. Its required config presupposes infrastructure this project does not have and will not have: `pulse_analytics_source` (posthog | mixpanel | custom), `pulse_tracing_source` (sentry | datadog | custom), `pulse_payments_source` (stripe | custom), plus `pulse_primary_event` / `pulse_value_event` naming events emitted by a hosted product with real users. This is a single static binary a user runs on their own machine against their own Twitch account — there is no telemetry pipeline, no user base, no payments, and the skill states it is "strictly about user experience and system performance" for such a product and explicitly "Does not report 'what shipped.'" The local SQLite DB cannot substitute: `pulse_db_enabled` is an optional supplement, and routing still requires the analytics

excluded_skills.name: ce-promote
excluded_skills.reason: Drafts launch/marketing copy — X posts, LinkedIn posts, email campaigns, blog intros, demo scripts — for a shipped feature. No lane in the owner's selection rule covers promotional or social copy, and there is no plausible use for a GPL-3.0 self-hosted Twitch points miner distributed as a single binary. Its enhanced path is bound to Spiral, Every's own hosted writing product (references/spiral-cli.md: `npx @every-env/spiral-cli@latest setup --pairing-code <code>`, device-code login against app.writewithspiral.com). The skill is honest that Spiral is optional and Path B drafts directly, but Path B is generic copywriting advice, not a project capability. The only marginally relevant output — a one-line changelog blurb — does not justify the skill.

excluded_skills.name: ce-proof
excluded_skills.reason: A client for Proof (https://www.proofeditor.ai), Every's hosted collaborative markdown editor. Its purpose is to upload local repository markdown — "a brainstorm, a unified plan, a learning, a draft" — to a third-party service and hand back a tokenized share URL. No lane in the selection rule covers hosted document publishing, and the mechanism is a real data-egress surface for a repo whose domain is Twitch OAuth device-code auth, persisted cookies, and Discord webhooks: `POST https://www.proofeditor.ai/share/markdown` needs no authentication, and the resulting doc is "ownerless until a signed-in Every user claims the doc", reachable by anyone holding the token. It also notes that emptying a doc "does **not** scrub comment marks", so content wipe is not privacy cleanup. Irrelevant hosted service with no plausible use here.

excluded_skills.name: ce-retune
excluded_skills.reason: Two independent disqualifiers. (1) Its Phase 0 gate is a hard refusal that this repo cannot satisfy: it demands "A run archive or a harness that produces one", "A build selector — the harness can point a run at a specific source checkout of the corpus", and "A repeatable task the corpus actually executes end to end", and instructs "If any is missing, **stop and say so**". This project has no skill-corpus benchmark harness, no per-run tool-call archive, and no A/B build selector, so every invocation terminates at Phase 0. (2) Even fully unblocked, its mutation target is wrong for this checkout: it audits and cuts prose across `./skills` (`references/cut-passes.md`: "one agent owns one skill directory and applies the class everywhere inside it"), which here is `.claude/skills/**` — vendored third-party bytes the repo holds at minimal local patching under three separate provider policies. A

excluded_skills.name: ce-riffrec-feedback-analysis
excluded_skills.reason: The consumption side of Riffrec (github.com/kieranklaassen/riffrec), a screen+voice+event capture tool whose `riffrec-*.zip` bundles are the intended input. This project has no user-feedback capture pipeline. Beyond relevance, the analyzer has two hard blockers verified in scripts/analyze_riffrec_zip.py: it shells out to `ffmpeg`/`ffprobe` for chunking and frame extraction (line 368 returns `"ffmpeg is not installed; cannot chunk media"`, and neither binary is present here), and transcription uploads the user's recorded media to a third-party paid API — line 317 posts to `"https://api.openai.com/v1/audio/transcriptions"` with `Authorization: Bearer {api_key}` from `OPENAI_API_KEY`, defaulting to model `gpt-4o-mini-transcribe`. It also "Always continue[s] into the `ce-brainstorm` skill" on the extensive path. Irrelevant tooling plus an out-of-scope provider dependency.

excluded_skills.name: ce-test-xcode
excluded_skills.reason: Builds and tests iOS apps on the macOS Simulator through the XcodeBuildMCP MCP server. Every step is Apple-platform-specific — `discover_projs`, `list_schemes`, `boot_simulator`, `build_ios_sim_app`, `install_app_on_simulator`, `launch_app_on_simulator`, `capture_sim_logs`, and a SwiftUI `AttributedString` tap limitation with an `xcrun simctl openurl` workaround. Its stated prerequisites are "Xcode installed with command-line tools", "XcodeBuildMCP MCP server connected", and "At least one iOS Simulator available", and it hard-stops otherwise: "Do NOT proceed until XcodeBuildMCP is confirmed working." This is a Linux Go project with no Apple surface; `xcodebuild` is absent. Irrelevant platform, no plausible use.
